scope: Dated public events, attributable public statements and separately labelled contextual primary/court/media evidence to 15 October 2026; not exhaustive. Social posts can enter chronology only as contextual reported events, never as eligible spoken claim cards. Midday 15 October pass adds Goa, cross-party outreach and court filings; the press source dates sometimes postdate events. Afternoon pass adds 12 dated association/mobilisation records; approximate media report dates are marked; future actions are not logged as completed.

events.title: Remarks in Supreme Court hearing
events.assessment: Reporting traces the movement’s origin to comments attributed to Chief Justice Surya Kant. The context and his subsequent clarification matter; protest slogans should not substitute for the full exchange.

events.title: Satirical CJP movement launches online
events.assessment: Abhijeet Dipke’s online post and subsequent CJP initiative begin circulating. Media reports the launch; no claim of formal electoral-party registration is made.

events.title: Founder gives early public interview
events.assessment: ThePrint profiles the satirical initiative and Dipke’s stated concern that younger citizens feel disconnected from politics.

events.title: Dipke answers questions in India Today interview
events.assessment: In an on-camera interview, the founder explains his objection to remarks attributed to the Chief Justice, youth frustration and intended peaceful protest. The unedited judicial hearing is a separate source requirement.

events.title: Bengaluru human-chain plan and permission refusal
events.assessment: Press reporting says police refused permission for a proposed 24 May Bengaluru human chain associated with the CJP name. No independent record of a completed human chain has been located; planned action is not counted as occurrence.

events.title: Platform and website restrictions contested
events.assessment: Indian Express examines withheld accounts, website access restrictions and CJP’s changing public identity. Attribution and legal rationale require original orders.

events.title: Bhushan publicly analyses CJP and urges careful street mobilisation
events.assessment: Reuters recorded a direct interview: he attributed CJP growth to youth discontent and urged careful offline organisation. Advice is not proof of an organisational directive.

events.title: CJP public press conference aired
events.assessment: ThePrint published a recording labelled as CJP's New Delhi press conference concerning the proposed 6 June protest. Specific claims from the recording remain excluded until reviewed against a time-coded transcript.

events.title: Then-spokesperson Dahiya interviewed ahead of June protest
events.assessment: A published interview features Vijeta Dahiya explaining the planned education protest. The video provides topic timestamps; specific claims await time-coded transcript verification.

events.title: First reported Jantar Mantar mobilisation
events.assessment: Students, exam aspirants and CJP supporters gather in Delhi; organisers demand accountability for examination failures.

events.title: Dipke addresses historical AAP work in interview
events.assessment: The Week Q&A records Dipke acknowledging a prior AAP role while denying current organisational ties as of June. Treat his denial as testimony, not an audited fact.

events.title: Periodic sit-ins and digital campaigning
events.assessment: The movement shifts from online satire to repeated public organising. The available chronology is a press reconstruction, not a complete daily attendance log.

events.title: Extended Jantar Mantar sit-in begins
events.assessment: Reported return for a sustained sit-in over examinations and ministerial accountability.

events.title: Call to NEET aspirants
events.assessment: Dipke appeals to exam aspirants to join the agitation after their examination obligations.

events.title: Candlelight vigil photographed at Jantar Mantar
events.assessment: EPA/Mihir Singh image and caption independently document a CJP supporter at a candlelight memorial vigil. Classified under Sharp #24 (symbolic lights) and #34 (vigils); the separate political mourning #43 category remains interpretive.
events.source: EPA photo via Lusa (agency photo ID 47333784)

events.title: Protest maintained, early attendance reported
events.assessment: Coverage describes persistent but still limited physical turnout. Crowd figures are press estimates and not audited totals.

events.title: Sonam Wangchuk begins hunger strike
events.assessment: Wangchuk joins demonstrators with students associated with AISA. His involvement is documented support, not proof of a single organisation controlling all participants.

events.title: Invitation extended across political parties
events.assessment: ThePrint quotes Dipke inviting all parties while rejecting electoral ambitions. A public invitation is distinct from a formal party alliance.

events.title: Congress organisational position examined
events.assessment: ThePrint reports Congress figures expressing solidarity while the party withheld a formal movement endorsement at that point.

events.title: Opposition and civil-society solidarity grows
events.assessment: Public figures visit or endorse parts of the agitation; formal organisational support varies among parties.

events.title: Wangchuk moved to hospital
events.assessment: Police intervention at the protest site and Wangchuk’s hospital transfer are reported; Dipke says he will continue the fast.

events.title: Large turnout before parliament march
events.assessment: Crowds begin gathering for the planned Sansad Chalo mobilisation the following day. Estimates remain source-dependent.

events.title: Sansad Chalo march and clashes
events.assessment: CJP-linked march, public-order operations, injuries and reported clashes. Police and protesters offer competing accounts; casualty and turnout figures are not independently reconciled.

events.title: CJP representatives meet J P Nadda
events.assessment: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are reported to have met the Union minister during the protest. This is a public negotiating contact.

events.title: Dipke publicly says a further Parliament march will continue
events.assessment: In a public reporter exchange near Jantar Mantar late Monday, Dipke forecasts another march on Tuesday. Later remarks changed the plan. This is a spoken intention, not evidence that the Tuesday march occurred.

events.title: AISF student book-stall dispute at CJP protest
events.assessment: PUCL Delhi's 21 July organisational statement alleges a police action against an AISF book stall at Jantar Mantar on 20 July. The independent police account and unedited footage are outstanding.

events.title: CJP publicly cancels further Parliament march citing injuries
events.assessment: At a news conference Dipke says CJP will not repeat the Parliament march after injuries. The decision modifies his earlier expressed plan rather than terminating every future CJP protest.

events.title: CJP removes Vijeta Dahiya from spokesperson role
events.assessment: Indian Express reports Dahiya's removal after a July 20 controversy. The shift is a dated organisational event and should not be mistaken for continued leadership or proof about disputed video sequences.

events.title: Dahiya disputes removal and discusses movement links in interview
events.assessment: In a named interview he describes the dismissal as surprising, contests accusations about his whereabouts and says he supports the cause without remaining a formal member.

events.title: SFI and DYFI solidarity protests in Chennai
events.assessment: Published rights documentation summarises Chennai arrests of SFI and DYFI protesters supporting the CJP-linked NEET campaign. An allied solidarity protest does not imply direct CJP oversight.

events.title: Government talks and shifting protest demands
events.assessment: The movement presses for the education minister’s resignation, FIR relief and assistance for affected students. Reported talks do not confirm implementation.

events.title: Wangchuk ends extended hunger strike
events.assessment: Coverage reports the end of his fast amid negotiations. The timing should be distinguished from later claims about who secured concessions.

events.title: Foreign ministry spokesperson declines to assess funding question
events.assessment: At a public press briefing, Randhir Jaiswal said he had no information on allegations of foreign financing to share. The statement is not proof of either financing or no financing.

events.title: Ministerial resignation officially accepted
events.assessment: The President’s communique confirms Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation and Pralhad Joshi’s additional Education charge. Whether CJP was the sole or determining cause is a separate causal assessment.

events.title: Ranka and Das detail plans in NDTV interview
events.assessment: Das describes an immediate grassroots agenda; Ranka declines to rule out his own eventual political career and describes the terms he understood from government negotiations. The subsequent written court order controls legal scope.

events.title: MEA fact-check rebuts exaggerated exoneration attributed to its spokesperson
events.assessment: The foreign ministry's fact-check unit called a viral account inaccurate for turning the July 24 statement into a declaration that CJP received no foreign funds. The correction is a written official intervention, not a new spoken CJP claim.

events.title: CJP press conference demands July FIR implementation
events.assessment: NDTV clips document a public demand for promised case withdrawals and an appeal for legal aid. The later Supreme Court order had defined terms and exceptions.

events.title: Supreme Court gives interim protest-related relief
events.assessment: Reporting describes protection for some students arrested in July demonstrations. The September written order is required for later and broader claims.

events.title: Dipke gives on-camera India Today interview
events.assessment: The founder rejects political proxy and foreign-backing allegations, discusses July 20 police actions and describes future grassroots organising. These are his reported positions, not independently audited funding claims.

events.title: Dipke sets out organisational intentions in Aaj Tak Q&A
events.assessment: The founder publicly discusses protest finance, political-party support, the paper-leak law and a 'response group' rather than immediate electoral entry. Statements remain the speaker's accounts unless separately verified.

events.title: Das is reported thanking AISF and SFI at CPI office
events.assessment: Organiser published a short quotation attributed to CJP's Saurav Das crediting student groups for help with protest organisation. Exact date and full recording of the remarks remain unverified; the site's political conclusions are not adopted.

events.title: Bhushan publicly discusses CJP as a civic mobilisation
events.assessment: At a Bengaluru university talk, Bhushan argued the movement had reduced fear of street protest. This is an attributed interpretation, not an independently measured impact.

events.title: Working committee and membership strategy announced at press conference
events.assessment: Dipke, Das and Ranka receive publicly reported roles. Das says the movement is recruiting online, is not currently fundraising and will not immediately register as an electoral party. Self-described financing remains unaudited.

events.title: 12-member working team publicly profiled
events.assessment: Indian Express reports the CJP office-bearers after a Maharashtra meeting and records its continued stated intention not to form a registered political party.

events.title: Past AAP associations reported
events.assessment: ThePrint identifies six CJP core members with former AAP ties or public support. Dipke and the AAP spokesperson deny a current organisational link; no command or funding relationship is established.

events.title: Supreme Court records mutual settlement
events.assessment: A dated court order closes July protest FIRs within specified terms and exceptions, orders a compensation framework, and records Saurav Das withdrawing a proposed 5 September march.

events.title: Proposed march withdrawn, per court record
events.assessment: Do not record the march as having occurred merely because older publicity announced it. The 1 September order captures the withdrawal.

events.title: CJP turns to election authority in Delhi press conference
events.assessment: Dipke, Das and Ranka announce demands concerning the CEC, election postponement, restoration of roll status and scrutiny of SIR files. Their allegations of wrongdoing are attributed, not proven.

events.title: New October mobilisation announced
events.assessment: Saurav Das is reported demanding protests beginning 10 October; alleged plans to arrest organisers are his attributed statement, not an established government plan.

events.title: Ranka previews civil disobedience and Jantar Mantar action
events.assessment: In an Indian Express interview, Ranka states that participants intend to sit wherever stopped and links further police force to demands for Home Minister's resignation.

events.title: CJP, AISA, AISF, SFI and AAP student wing share public briefing
events.assessment: The joint New Delhi press conference called for sustained national mobilisation against the CEC and electoral-roll changes. The Free Press Journal also identifies ASAP, AAP's student wing, as a participant.
events.source: PTI/IANS / Free Press Journal press-conference report

events.title: Bengaluru speeches clarify distinct positions
events.assessment: At a CJP-associated Freedom Park protest, Dhruv Rathee publicly denies regime-change intent for himself; Prakash Raj alleges election-official direction by ministers. Both statements remain separately attributed.

events.title: AAP CM Bhagwant Mann acknowledges Dipke's former party work
events.assessment: At India Today's Panchayat event, Mann confirmed Dipke worked previously in AAP's social-media team and rejected the accusation of current AAP control of CJP.

events.title: Public-order restrictions scrutinised
events.assessment: Reports describe a Supreme Court hearing on extensive Delhi travel restrictions before planned CJP demonstrations. Reported judicial remarks must not be overstated as a final liability finding.

events.title: Dipke addresses Loksamvad and outlines October protest
events.assessment: During a public event reported by The Indian Express, Dipke argues that transport restrictions are disproportionate, repeats the 13-crore roll figure and rejects an immediate plan to register a political party.

events.title: Goa authorities refuse permission for an 11 October gathering
events.assessment: Report citing the North Goa district order says organisers applied on 7 October and permission was declined on 9 October. A previous protester's unrelated placard was among police-cited concerns; that does not prove a CJP position about the named individuals on it.
events.source: Jansatta / Indian Express report of Goa order

events.title: Kejriwal issues public appeal for CJP-called October 10 protest
events.assessment: The Times of India attributes an appeal to Kejriwal urging participation and stating his intention to attend with his family. Intention and presence must not be conflated.

events.title: Delhi protest restrictions and detentions
events.assessment: Reuters reports large-scale preventive measures, transport disruption and arrests before a CJP-backed rally targeting the CEC. Police figures and protest figures differ.

events.title: Nitin Nabin alleges an external destabilisation plot
events.assessment: At a Delhi BJP press conference, Nabin alleged that groups involving the opposition and CJP acted at the behest of unnamed foreign forces. The publisher reports no publicly supplied documentation establishing direction or financing.
events.source: Times of India / filmed press conference

events.title: Saket court declines Ratna Singh's police-FIR application on procedural grounds
events.assessment: A magistrate dismissed Singh's application concerning alleged restraint, citing defects in affidavit, officer identification and jurisdiction. This is not a finding that confinement did or did not happen, or that police conduct was lawful.

events.title: Yadav, Bhushan and Neha Bora join protest march near INA Market
events.assessment: Outlook's PTI-captioned photograph shows Yogendra Yadav, Prashant Bhushan, AISA leader Neha Bora and CPI(ML) leader Dipankar Bhattacharya leading a march during the CJP protest day. Co-presence is evidenced, formal coalition management is not.

events.title: Pune student activists headed to Delhi protest detained at Itarsi
events.assessment: Indian Express reports members of AISF and other student campaigns were held en route; allegations about grounds and circumstances require police records and court orders.

events.title: Further demonstrations after releases
events.assessment: Reuters reports continued action, court activity and competing accounts of treatment of demonstrators, journalists and lawyers.

events.title: CJP leaders raise mobile-seizure and police-conduct allegations at briefing
events.assessment: Das and Ranka address reporters after release. Their claims about device custody and possible cloning remain allegations; a forensic examination, seizure documents and any independent judicial finding are outstanding.

events.title: Ratna Singh describes nine-hour detention at CJP press conference
events.assessment: Legal-affairs head Singh says she was held in her vehicle and was told officers had orders from above. The News Minute identifies the speaker; another report appears to misattribute the account to Ashutosh Ranka. Police logs remain outstanding.
events.source: The News Minute / Press Club interview

events.title: Bangla Sahib events prompt disputed policing and sanctity allegations
events.assessment: At a CJP press conference Das alleges police entered Bangla Sahib with batons and removed sheltering protesters. Separate DSGMC claims concern AAP-linked participants. Both sets of allegations remain disputed; actor identities and command chains should not be conflated.

events.title: Goa CJP-linked protest and seven detentions
events.assessment: Coverage says seven demonstrators were detained at Panaji's Azad Maidan despite denial of permission; a court reportedly directed their release that night. The Goa affiliate's participants are not automatically proved to act on national CJP instructions. Obtain the order and verified organiser identity.

events.title: Delhi Police denotifies Jantar Mantar as protest venue
events.assessment: An October 12 police notification names Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternatives. Subsequent petitions dispute the change; a challenge is not a judicial invalidation.

events.title: Ranka interviewed after October protests and detentions
events.assessment: In a Hindustan Times edited Q&A, Ranka disputes police interpretations of peace bonds and describes custody, a strategy review, and opposition relationships. Original bond and arrest records remain outstanding.

events.title: Dhruv Rathee explicitly disavows CJP organisational membership
events.assessment: In a published filmed public statement, Rathee says he is not joining or formally affiliated with CJP. Public protest participation must not be mislabelled as party office, funding or instruction.

events.title: Rahul Gandhi describes parallel protests as one cause
events.assessment: At a public press conference, Gandhi said separate demonstrations shared an anti-CEC objective and alleged top-level pressure on the commissioner. The allegations have not been independently proved; the shared cause is not evidence of a combined operational hierarchy.

events.title: CJP organisers enter disputed protest site
events.assessment: Coverage describes Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das arriving at Jantar Mantar despite restrictions. Participants dispute the police account of their conduct.

events.title: Congress reportedly attempts invitation to CJP leader
events.assessment: Indian Express cites unnamed Congress and intermediary sources describing an attempted invitation via Prashant Bhushan to Rahul Gandhi's high tea. The report does not establish Dipke attended, accepted, entered any agreement or took instructions; reported contact should not be upgraded to a structural alliance.

events.title: Five-day custody ordered
events.assessment: Reuters and Indian Express report a magistrate ordering custody for Ranka and Das. This is a procedural court action, not a conviction.

events.title: Ajinkya Shinde responds publicly after custody and bond decision
events.assessment: Released on a personal bond, Shinde tells reporters CJP will not be deterred. Police and the defence give differing legal interpretations of prior undertakings; custody does not determine guilt.

events.title: Nagpur press interaction: independence and court allegations
events.assessment: Dipke tells reporters CJP is an independent pressure group, says he had no specific discussion with Rahul Gandhi, disputes policing explanations, and criticises courts without identifying particular party-symbol cases.

events.title: Denotification challenged in two courts
events.assessment: Supreme Court and Delhi High Court petitions challenge the October 12 change of protest site. Reporting identifies an open dispute, not a final ruling on legality.

events.title: Election-roll dispute remains unresolved
events.assessment: Reuters details allegations of large-scale exclusion and the election authority’s denial of partisan bias. A final-voter disenfranchisement total has not been audited here.

events.title: Delhi CM Gupta publicly alleges CJP–AAP alignment
events.assessment: At a Delhi press conference, Rekha Gupta calls CJP an AAP 'B party'. This is a reported public allegation, not independent evidence of a financing or instruction chain.

events.title: Dipke announces planned 16 October Connaught Place gathering
events.assessment: Press reporting attributes a public call for a 16 October flag demonstration to Dipke. The announcement is not evidence that the future gathering occurred.

events.title: Moitra describes solidarity without merged protest timetables
events.assessment: In an India Today interview, TMC MP Mahua Moitra backs protest rights while describing distinct opposition mobilisation schedules; shared demands do not establish a centralised CJP leadership chain.

events.title: CJP West Zone coordinator Rohit Patel appears in televised protest debate
events.assessment: India Today identifies CJP West Zone coordinator Rohit Patel alongside SFI representative Aishi Ghosh, Congress spokesperson Rahul Singh and BJP's Ajay Alok. Joint television appearance is not evidence of organisational merger.

events.title: American singer publishes uncorroborated donor accusation
events.assessment: Mary Millben alleges US donor support for CJP on X, according to reporting. No authenticated donor names, transfers, FCRA filings or AEI instructions are supplied. The origin is a written social post, EXCLUDED from spoken-claim register.
events.source: Times of India / coverage of written X post

events.title: Delhi Police and Union Home Secretary set out court affidavits
events.assessment: Anurag Kumar's affidavit alleges past protest restrictions were breached and says detainees were held in temporary centres. Home Secretary Govind Mohan apologises to the Supreme Court while defending a 9–10 October cellular-internet suspension within four kilometres of Raisina Hill. These are submitted government positions, not the court's rulings.
events.source: Indian Express / reporting on filed affidavits

events.title: Delhi High Court agrees to hear challenge to planned 16 October protest
events.assessment: Court reportedly agrees to hear a petition seeking to prevent the announced Connaught Place action. Listing or agreeing to hear a petition does not mean a ban has been issued; preserve the 16 October gathering as future and unverified.

events.title: Yogendra Yadav openly advocates synchronisation without a central command
events.assessment: Extended Federal Q&A says parallel mobilisations now need more deliberate coordination, enumerating separate parties, youth groups and unaffiliated citizens. Prospective advocacy is not evidence of previous central planning.
